history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: this row says Jamnagar, but the Dwarkadhish Temple stands at Dwarka in Devbhumi Dwarka district, about 130 km west of Jamnagar; the town has been corrected. Archaeological findings suggest an original temple as early as 200 BCE (tradition credits Vajranabha, Krishna's great-grandson); the structure was destroyed by Mahmud Begada in 1473 and the present five-storied temple, supported by 72 pillars with a spire of about 78 m, was rebuilt and enlarged in the 15th-16th century in Maru-Gurjara (Chalukyan) style. It is one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites, the 98th Divya Desam, and the seat of the Dwarka Sharada Matha, one of the four peeths established by Adi Shankaracharya, who visited the shrine (a memorial inside commemorates his visit). Sources: Wikipedia, dwarkadhish.org, templetimings.in.

name: Dwarkadhish Temple
town_description: Dwarka is an ancient coastal city on the Okhamandal peninsula at the mouth of the Gomti river, counted among the Sapta Puri (seven most sacred Hindu cities) and the Char Dham. Legend holds it was Krishna's capital, said to have been reclaimed from the sea.

travel.airport: Jamnagar Airport (~137 km); Porbandar is an alternative
travel.railway: Dwarka railway station (DWK), on the Okha-Ahmedabad line
travel.road: Roads from Jamnagar (~137 km), Rajkot and Ahmedabad; entry via Moksha Dwar, exit toward Gomti Ghat via Swarga Dwar

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Janmashtami draws lakhs of pilgrims
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:30 AM - 1:00 PM and 5:00 PM - 9:30 PM daily; closed 1:00-5:00 PM for Anosar (the deity's afternoon rest)
